title: Prototype deployment playbook and stakeholder sprint log
body:
Purpose: quick, pragmatic playbook to run the prototype deployment phase for customer X (internal name: BlueMarlin). This doc combines the sprint task tracker, workshop notes, known constraints, and acceptance criteria for finishing POC milestone 1 (end-to-end inference + billing demo).

High level objective:
- Deliver a reproducible deployment that demonstrates: 1) 50 qps sustained on a 4-GPU Dedicated pool, 2) <120ms p50 generation for 256-token prompts, 3) a demo showing autoscaling and fallback to hosted variant.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Aisha Patel (owner) — SE lead, overall delivery, customer coordination
- Marco Chen — infra engineer, deployment scripts, GPU tuning
- Priya Nambiar — product PM, acceptance criteria and demo script
- Liam O'Connor — security reviewer, VPC and KMS integration
- Evelyn Ruiz — solutions QA, scenario tests + regression set
- Customer PM: Daniel Park — approves demo acceptance

Sprint cadence (3-week sprint plan):
- Week 0 (prep, milestone gating): environment access, credentials, Jira triage, risk call
- Week 1 (baseline deploy): provision Dedicated pool, nail down model variant, run smoke tests
- Week 2 (performance tuning): kernels/quantization tuning, batching profiles, prefix cache config
- Week 3 (demo polish & runbook): produce demo script, fallback test, run acceptance test suite

Top-level tasks (owner | ETA | status):
- Provision Dedicated test pool | Marco | 2024-11-01 | in_progress
- Confirm model variant + quantization profile | Marco/Priya | 2024-11-03 | todo
- Implement autoscale policy (min 1 max 4) | Marco | 2024-11-05 | todo
- VPC peering and KMS key exchange | Liam | 2024-11-06 | todo
- End-to-end smoke test: sample prompts + billing signal | Evelyn | 2024-11-08 | todo
- Workshop w/ customer: runbook dry-run | Aisha/Priya | 2024-11-09 | scheduled
- Regression harness: 30 prompt set | Evelyn | 2024-11-10 | todo
- Demo rehearsal (internal) | All | 2024-11-11 | scheduled

Acceptance criteria (must be green for milestone sign-off):
- Functional: model produces expected intent extraction and top-3 answers for canonical prompts (see regression set).
- Perf: sustained 50 qps for 10 minutes without queueing, p50 <120ms for 256 tokens, p95 <450ms.
- Reliability: fallback to hosted variant triggers within 10s if Dedicated pool unavailable, with no silent failures.
- Security: VPC peering validated, audit logs available for the demo window, KMS encryption of keys confirmed.
- Demo: scripted customer scenario executed end-to-end by SE without engineer intervention.

Risk register (likelihood x impact):
- Delayed GPU provisioning (medium x high): contingency — run limited-capacity demo on hosted with explicit note, escalate to infra on day+1.
- Model mismatch / hallucination in regressions (high x medium): contingency — lock to a safer model variant and surface to customer as known tradeoff.
- VPC peering policy rejection from customer security (low x high): contingency — schedule a joint security call and provide architecture diagram + SOC2 evidence.

Workshop agenda (90m, customer-facing dry run):
- 0-10m: Introductions + objective alignment (Aisha)
- 10-25m: Architecture walkthrough (Marco + Liam)
- 25-50m: Live deploy checklist & roles (Priya)
- 50-75m: Hands-on run: trigger demo, show fallback, inspect logs (Evelyn)
- 75-90m: Open Q&A, next steps, signoff criteria

Open questions (owner / note):
- Customer rate profile: confirm bursty vs steady (Daniel) — pending answer from customer workspace.
- Billing demo hook: which billing event should we simulate? (Priya) — prefer usage-based invoice event.
- Model variant floor: does customer require L2-norm QA? (Marco) — follow-up with applied-ml if needed.

Diagnostics & observability checklist for workshop:
- Console route dashboard: token and latency charts pinned to demo route
- Per-request trace binding to demo id
- Canary logs exported to customer S3 for postmortem
- Alerting: p50/p95 breach pager threshold set to 2x expected baseline

Quick runbook excerpt (for SE during demo):
1) Warm cache: run 5 high-priority prefix prompts to populate KV cache.
2) Start load generator at 10 qps and step to 50 qps over 90s.
3) Trigger simulated Dedicated pool failover (toggle capacity in console) and verify fallback within 10s.
4) Capture trace id and download request/response payloads to share with customer.

Version history / notes:
- 2024-10-28: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-10-30: added risk register and acceptance criteria (Marco)
- 2024-11-05: updated perf targets after kernel tuning run (Marco/Evelyn)
- 2024-11-12: prep for customer dry-run, clarified workshop agenda (Aisha)

Next immediate actions (today):
- Marco: confirm Dedicated pool quota and post screenshot in Slack #poc-blue-marlin by EOD
- Liam: request KMS key exchange template from security and share with customer sec contact
- Priya: confirm billing demo event and update linked demo script in Confluence

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep demo tight — three canonical flows only. Avoid branching logic on stage.
- If perf is marginal, bias toward demonstrating autoscale and graceful fallback rather than raw throughput.
- Collect one customer quote during workshop for postmortem and case study permission.

Attachments and artifacts to prepare before customer session:
- Lightweight runbook PDF (1 page)
- Demo script with exact prompts and expected outputs (Confluence link)
- Short video recording of the internal rehearsal

End of playbook.
